content.text: No exclusivity or sourcing obligation binds AbbVie anywhere; the only exclusivity runs in our favour. Submitting a compliant finding.

input.quote: 5.8.1 Harpoon shall not, and shall cause its Affiliates not to (a) directly or indirectly, develop, commercialize or otherwise exploit any Competing Product in any country or other jurisdiction in the Territory, or (b) license, authorize, appoint, or otherwise enable any Third Party to directly or indirectly, develop, commercialize or otherwise exploit any Competing Product in any country or other jurisdiction in the Territory, except, in each case ((a) and (b)), as otherwise expressly provided in this Agreement.
input.rationale: The Agreement meets the preferred position: no exclusivity, sole-supplier or requirements obligation is imposed on AbbVie. Section 5.8 ("Exclusivity with Respect to the Territory") runs entirely in our favour — it binds Harpoon and its Affiliates not to develop, commercialize or license Competing Products in the Territory (p0368), with only Harpoon-side acquisition/change-of-control carve-outs that additionally give AbbVie discretionary information-shut-off and JGC-disbandment rights (p0369). The exclusive licences in Section 5.1.3 are grants to AbbVie (p0355–p0356), and Harpoon's retained rights in 5.6.1 are expressly subject to Section 5.8. Elsewhere AbbVie is affirmatively free to use third parties: it may appoint distributors "in its sole discretion" (5.4, p0360), co-promote or appoint Third Parties to promote (5.5, p0361), and has the first right to take third-party in-licences (5.9.2, p0372). Searches for requirements/sole-supply, third-party procurement bars and AbbVie-side non-compete language returned nothing binding AbbVie. Per the detection guidance, exclusivity granted to the Customer is acceptable and is not flagged; the Harpoon-side non-compete is also addressed under NONCOMPETE and is not double-flagged here.
